title: Figure with Source Information

illustrates.quote:
c. When an illustration has a source citation, place it immediately following the caption using 7-5 margins. If a description of the illustration is required, begin the source citation on the line following the description.
e. When both a print caption and a transcriber-generated description are needed, begin the description (enclosed in transcriber’s note indicators) on the line following the caption.

figure.description: A diver with an air bag and a valve. The diver is wearing a full body diving suit, fins, cap, and a mask.

blocks.description: A diver with an air bag and a valve. The diver is wearing a full body diving suit, fins, cap, and a mask.

blocks.text: Figure 7-1 **Diving's early history.** In the mid 1600s the extremely inventive Italian scientist Giovanni Borelli was the first to visualize a diver as a free-swimming frogman, complete with swim fins.
blocks.features: 'Diving's early history.' is bold; 'Figure 7-1' and the rest of the caption are plain.

blocks.text: Courtesy of Historical Diving Society, USA
blocks.features: Source citation, printed above the placeholder box; braille places it after the description per 6.2.2c.

print.notes: The photograph itself is copyrighted and replaced in print with a placeholder box reading 'Copyrighted Image' (figure.labels); the caption sits to its left, and the source citation sits above the box. The transcriber nonetheless supplies a description of what the (unreproduced) photo depicts, per 6.2.2e — unlike example-6-1/6-2's figure.description, this one IS built as a separate transcriber's-note block, confirmed by forward translation matching the agreed braille exactly.

braille.notes: The caption starts in cell 7 (6 spaces) with runovers in cell 5 (4 spaces). The transcriber's note containing the description follows in the same 7-5 margins. The source citation follows, also in 7-5, per 6.2.2c. No transcriber's-note label is needed (or given) because the caption itself begins with the identifying word 'Figure' (6.2.2b).

resolution: A and B agreed byte-for-byte, but BOTH share the same margin defect (exactly the 'agreement is no evidence' risk flagged in the task): the caption's margins are given as 5/3 instead of 6/4, and the description's and citation's margins as 4/2 instead of 6/4. This was caught by decoding the raw source text directly (source-6.txt lines 4783-4793 carry the book's own per-line numbering, e.g. '4    ', '10   ', stripped here with a small script, engine/brf-ascii.mjs's unicodeBrailleToBrf used to decode the Unicode braille glyphs to BRF ASCII) rather than by trusting either run: every one of the three blocks' own first line in the raw source begins with exactly 6 Unicode braille-blank cells (U+2800) after its line-number prefix, and every runover with exactly 4, confirmed byte-for-byte. The print text content of all three blocks (caption, description, citation) was independently confirmed correct in both runs by forward-translating each verbatim through Emboss's translator and matching the corrected braille exactly, including the bold passage on 'Diving's early history.' (confirmed by forward-translating with that span marked TF_BOLD; neither run's caption text carried a features/markup field for it, corrected here). The citation ('Courtesy of Historical Diving Society, USA') is recorded as kind 'other' and is expected to be dropped by buildModel6, not built — matching F-168 (source citations/credits inside an imggroup are lost by Emboss).
